cur:catacombs-ponziano-bust-of-christ.summary: Christ appears as a frontal bust with a cross-nimbus, large eyes, short beard and long hair, set within an arched frame above a painted inscription. The austere, hieratic face belongs to the age of icons and shows how the catacombs continued to be decorated for pilgrims long after burials there had ceased.
facts: Commons dates the painting to about the 6th–7th century, from Wilpert's 1903 plate.
The Catacomb of Pontian, on the Via Portuense, is also known for a painted baptistery and frescoes of the martyrs Abdon and Sennen.
Painting reproduced from Joseph Wilpert, Die Malereien der Katakomben Roms (Freiburg, 1903), whose plates were photographed in the catacombs and hand-coloured in front of the originals.

cur:monumental-naples-baptistery-peter-o.summary: A haloed, beardless Christ in white stands at the left, turned towards a blue sea full of fish, where a figure in the water reaches towards him; above, a man sits in a boat. The incomplete scene has been read as the Miraculous Draught of Fishes, as Christ saving Peter from the waves, or as the calling of Peter and Andrew.
facts: Of the scenes once set within garlands around the dome, four survive: the Traditio Legis, the Samaritan woman with the Wedding at Cana, the Miraculous Draught (or Peter on the water), and the women at the tomb.

The baptistery of San Giovanni in Fonte beside Naples Cathedral is one of the oldest in the West; its building is dated to the 4th century, and its construction is attributed to Bishop Severus (362–408) or to later bishops.

cur:monumental-naples-baptistery-peter-o.notes: The exact Gospel episode is uncertain; scholars propose the Miraculous Draught, Peter walking on the water, a combination of both, or the calling of Peter and Andrew.
